description: A disk cache and Parquet archive for Databento.CSharpApiClient, so each day of Databento data is paid for once. The client's time-series calls served from per-symbol UTC day files, batch jobs for large ranges, a compactor that folds day files into Parquet any reader can query, and backup and restore of the whole cache.
releaseNotes:
v1.6.2 - 2026-11-28

Fixed
- A time-series call opens a day file by name instead of listing its month folder first. On a folder of 58,800
  day files a symbol-day read took 51 to 66 ms and allocated 25 MB; it now takes 1.6 to 5.6 ms and 177 KB.

v1.6.1 - 2026-11-27

Changed
- The download request log line writes its window half-open, [start to end), as Databento reads it, and names a
  single UTC day once. Its structured FirstDay and LastDay properties become one Days string.

v1.6.0 - 2026-11-27

Added
- EnsureCachedAsync (and the sync EnsureCached): makes sure the cache holds a range of symbol-days and returns no
  records. Cached days are found by day file name and archive index with no record read; only the others are downloaded,
  as a CacheMode.Use call would. Returns an EnsureCachedReport of what was cached, saved and still missing.

Changed
- The per-day Debug lines name the file without its folder.

Fixed
- An archive read no longer reopens its file and parses its whole Parquet footer: each file is kept open with its index.
  One symbol-day read of an SPXW cbbo-1m month went from 0.8 s and 85 MB allocated to 2 to 3 ms and under 2 MB.
- Shut the application down before a restore. A restore refuses, naming them, while archive files are open (best effort,
  Windows), and checks once more just before it swaps the backup in.

v1.5.0 - 2026-11-27

Added
- SettleDelay (default 15 minutes, up to 24 hours): a downloaded day is saved only once its UTC day has ended plus
  this delay, so a day Databento is still finalizing is not locked in.
- AvailableEndRefusal (ServeEmpty by default, or Throw), AvailableEndRefreshInterval (default 15 minutes, on a UTC
  grid) and CheckAvailabilityFirst (default false, the 1.4.1 metadata-first flow).
- Empty days and Bypass replacements are saved only when Databento's condition for the day is available.

Changed
- A time-series download goes straight to Databento with no dataset range or conditions read before it. A request
  refused past the available end is cut there and sent once more; the end is remembered and later requests are cut
  before they are sent. Days past the end are served empty and not saved by default.
- Depends on Databento.CSharpApiClient 2.8.0.
- Compactor log lines: a line as listing starts, counts with thousands separators, dry run and delta folding worded.

v1.4.1 - 2026-11-26

Changed
- Log messages end without a period, which read as part of a path or a name before it; a step under way ends
  with " ..." instead.

v1.4.0 - 2026-11-26

Added
- Diagnostic logging through Microsoft.Extensions.Logging: a Logger (ILogger, default NullLogger.Instance) on
  CachedDatabentoClientOptions, ArchiveCompactorOptions, CacheBackupOptions and CacheRestoreOptions. Information:
  each download from Databento and what it brought back, batch jobs, and the steps of a compaction, backup and
  restore. Debug: each symbol-day served from its day file or the archive or not cached, and each save or why a
  day was not saved. Warning and Error: failures, refusals, unreadable files. Nothing is formatted below the
  logger's level, and the message text is culture-invariant. A logger's methods shall not throw; the package
  drops anything they throw, so a failing logger never changes what the cache serves or writes.

Changed
- Depends on Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions 8.0.3.
- Built on Databento.CSharpApiClient 2.7.2, which reads a JSON array one record at a time as it arrives.

Fixed
- A day file is handed to the client as it is decompressed, and its records parsed one at a time, instead of the
  whole day held several times over on the large object heap. A compaction of many groups at once reached
  gigabytes: on invented cbbo-1s days sized like an SPXW month, 12 groups at once peaked at a 4.4 GB GC heap
  (3.4 GB LOH) before and under 1 GB (69 MB LOH) after, allocating 102 GB instead of 342 GB.

v1.3.0 - 2026-11-25

Added
- Databento's metadata and symbology calls on the cached client, passed through uncached: ListDatasets,
  ListSchemas, ListPublishers, ListFields, ListUnitPrices, GetDatasetCondition, GetDatasetRange, ListConditions,
  GetRecordCount, GetBillableSize, GetCost and ResolveSymbols, so one client serves the whole Historical API.
  Async on ICachedDatabentoClient, with default implementations that throw NotSupportedException; their
  synchronous forms are in CachedDatabentoClientExtensions.

Changed
- Built on Databento.CSharpApiClient 2.7.1.
- The DBN client is created only when Transport is Dbn; with the default Json it held an unused one.

v1.2.0 - 2026-11-25

Added
- CacheMode.CacheOnly: serves what the cache holds and downloads nothing, so a call never costs anything. When
  the cache lacks a symbol-day of the range, the call throws NotCachedException naming them, and asks Databento
  nothing. For a restored backup used as it is, or a host that must not reach Databento for a while.

v1.1.0 - 2026-11-25

Added
- ICachedDatabentoClient, which CachedDatabentoClient implements: the time-series calls with a CacheMode, the
  batch calls and the ArchiveFileUnreadable event, so code can be handed a fake in tests. An implementation
  writes only the 11 async calls for several symbols; CachedDatabentoClientExtensions adds the one-symbol and
  sync forms.
- CachedDatabentoClient is an IDatabentoTimeseriesClient (client 2.7.0) and serves its calls from the cache
  (CacheMode.Use), so code that takes either Databento client takes the cache too. The cache still refuses
  ALL_SYMBOLS: it needs the raw symbols.

Changed
- Built on Databento.CSharpApiClient 2.7.0 (it was 2.6.0).

v1.0.0 - 2026-11-24

First release.
- CachedDatabentoClient: the client's time-series calls for cbbo-1s, cbbo-1m, bbo-1s, bbo-1m, tcbbo, trades,
  ohlcv-1s/1m/1h/1d and statistics, async and sync, served per symbol and UTC day from the cache, else
  downloaded whole, and saved before the call returns once Databento says the day is final. JSON or DBN
  transport, a Bypass mode that downloads again, and empty days saved only when symbology confirms the symbol
  was not listed (by default).
- Batch jobs for ranges too large for the time-series calls, with a cost cap and reuse of a job that already
  covers the range; any Databento batch download folder can be ingested too.
- DatabentoArchiveCompactor: folds day files into one Parquet archive per dataset, schema, group and month,
  checked record by record (by default) before the files it replaces are deleted.
- DatabentoCacheBackup and DatabentoCacheRestore: the whole cache as one checked tar in an IBackupStore, with
  retention, a dry run, and a restore that refuses while the cache is in use.

Full history: https://github.com/mrut2pac/Databento.CSharpApiClient.Caching/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
